Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain in right knee; several weeks of right knee pain after injury jamming into the corner of a table 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Oblique tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with underlying subchondral edema.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 12 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Oblique tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with underlying subchondral edema.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Tendinitis rotuliana izquierda.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones.
Condropatía rotuliana superficial.
Engrosamiento y aumento de señal del tercio proximal del tendón rotuliano con rotura parcial de
las fibras centrales y laterales con discreto edema de la grasa de Hoffa adyacente.
Tendón cuadricipital, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda de tibial dentro de
límites normales.
Aumento de señal de las partes blandas entre la banda iliotibial y el cóndilo femoral lateral.
Impresión:
Condropatía rotuliana superficial.
Leve tendinosis rotuliana proximal con roturas parciales de las fibras centrales bilaterales. Discreto
edema de la grasa de Hoffa adyacente.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Small joint effusion.
6.3 cm popliteal cyst with a trace of edema extending both superiorly and inferiorly consistent with partial rupture.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Small marginal osteophytes in keeping with mild medial compartment osteoarthrosis.
Full-thickness focal chondral loss at the mid medial femoral condyle.
Intrasubstance mucoid degeneration of the medial meniscus, with degenerative meniscal tear; oblique tear at the junction of the body and posterior horn, with a posterior root avulsion.
Normal MCL. Mild semimembranosus tendinosis.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Tiny partial radial tear of the body. Undisplaced oblique tear within the posterior horn. Background of intrasubstance mucoid degeneration and discoid meniscus.
Normal articular cartilage. No established osteoarthrosis.
Normal lateral collateral ligament structures.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Mucoid degeneration of both the ACL and PCL.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Small marginal osteophytes in keeping with mild patellofemoral compartment osteoarthrosis.
Full-thickness focal cartilage fissuring at the median patellar ridge as well as the at the medial trochlea articular cartilage with mild underlying subchondral reactive bone marrow signal changes.

Bones:
Reactive bone marrow signal changes, as above.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
1.Mild medial tibiofemoral and patellofemoral compartment osteoarthrosis.
2.Severe intrasubstance degeneration of the medial and lateral menisci, with degenerative tearing.
3.Large popliteal cyst, with features of recent partial rupture.

Findings:  There is a mild knee effusion. Myxoid degeneration of the body of medial meniscus is noted but no definite tear. Normal lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  Normal tibiofemoral articular cartilage. Mild fraying of the lateral patellar facet articular cartilage is noted. The patellofemoral articular cartilage is otherwise well maintained. Normal visualized bones and surrounding soft tissues.  
Conclusion: Myxoid degeneration of the medial meniscal body but no definite tear.

FINDINGS:

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
High-grade, likely functionally complete tear of the femoral attachment of the medial collateral ligament with near complete involvement of the superficial and complete tear is of the deep meniscofemoral fibers and attachment.
Periligamentous edema.
The medial meniscus and the articular cartilage are unremarkable.

Normal.

None

CONCLUSION:
1.High-grade, likely functionally complete tear of the femoral insertion of the medial collateral ligament as detailed above. For correlation with valgus instability on exam. Consider orthopedic surgery assessment.
2.Low-grade injury of the anterior cruciate ligament distally.
3.Small focal impaction injury/fracture of the lateral femoral condyle.
4.Minimal superficial infrapatellar bursitis.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Mild to moderate joint effusion. There is a small popliteal cyst measuring 1.3 cm x 0.7 cm x 1.6 cm (AP x T x CC)

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
There is horizontal tear involving the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus surfacing inferiorly. There is a small meniscal flap in the medial tibial gutter with reactive subjacent tibial bone marrow edema. A second meniscal flap is seen in the posterior intercondylar notch adjacent to the posterior root measuring 1.2 cm. The medial meniscus is mildly extruded. There are adjacent small Parameniscal cysts posteriorly.
There is complete tear of the medial collateral ligament, involving both the deep and superficial components at the femoral attachment with mild retraction. The femoral attachment of the medial patellofemoral ligament is also likely injured with adjacent edema.
There is mild to moderate cartilage thinning.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
No meniscal tear is identified.
Lateral collateral ligament complex is intact.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
The posterior cruciate ligament demonstrates irregularity and increased signal intensity likely representing high-grade tear. There a few residual fibers, but this could be functionally complete tear. There is edematous changes around the meniscofemoral ligament likely representing sprain.
Anterior cruciate ligament is intact.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
There is small bony fragments at the medial attachment of patellar ligament with minimal to mild bone marrow changes likely representing remote Osgood-Schlatter.
There is diffuse mild to moderate cartilage thinning with focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the trochlea.

Bones:
There is associated bone marrow edema involving the medial femoral epicondyle, with possible mild impaction within the posterior aspect. Bone marrow changes within the medial aspect of the fibula likely associated with degenerative changes.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
1.Horizontal tear involving the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with associated parameniscal cyst and two meniscal flap, as detailed above.
2.Complete tear of the medial collateral ligament involving both the deep and superficial components.
3.High-grade tear involving the posterior cruciate ligament, which could be functionally complete tear. There is associated meniscofemoral ligament sprain.
4.Bone contusion involving lateral femoral condyle with possible mild impaction fracture within the posterior aspect.
5.Chronic fragment with mild marrow changes at the tibial attachment of patellar ligament likely representing remote Osgood-Schlatter with mild active stress changes.
6.Mild to moderate chondropathy involving medial and patellofemoral compartment.
